catalog_item_supersession.design_decision: Declared exactly as design ADR 0009's 2026-09-25 amendment ('Superseded catalog items and native-id merge') names it, so catalog-api can code its merge steps 4-7 to the record. The resolution is a function rather than a view because it is defined for any native id, including ids with no catalog_items row (activity.impressions.item_id and the outcome endpoint record ids verbatim); a view keyed on catalog_items would drop those or push the COALESCE into every reader. catalog_item_moves carries from_item_id and to_item_id beside the amendment's columns, so a revert moves a row back only while it still points at to_item_id.

ledger.erasure: personal data keyed to user_id: the erasure procedure deletes a user's rows and export includes them; deleting the users row cascades

catalog_item_supersession.note: A superseded catalog item keeps its catalog_items row; a supersession row records its current survivor, closed by valid_to on revert. Resolution is always one hop: when a survivor is itself superseded, the writer closes the old row and opens one to the new survivor naming the compressing row as via_id. graph.catalog_item excludes currently superseded items. This repository declares the shape only; catalog-api writes every row inside the ADR 0014 transactions and enforces that both items share a kind.

resolution.meaning: the survivor_id of native_id's current supersession row, or native_id itself when there is none; one probe of the current-survivor index

supersessions.decision_ref: the matching decision row for edition_promotion, the admin_audit_log entry for catalog_reattachment; not a foreign key

compatibility.destructive_changes: require a new major contract and an explicit migration
compatibility.rollback: every destructive migration requires a tested rollback or restore procedure

columns.loader_extraction_latch.generation: BIGINT NULL (legacy rows retain NULL until the loader cutover)

extraction_latch.design_decision: Named public.loader_extraction_latch and shaped with a loader discriminator so the loader family can share one relation, matching discogs-sql-loader's tableinator/extraction_latch.py startup probe: it checks public.loader_extraction_latch against information_schema, requires the loader column (REQUIRED_COLUMNS) along with the other non-key columns at their exact information_schema types, and scopes every statement to loader = 'discogs' (its own _key_columns() and ON CONFLICT (loader, version)). It verifies via pg_constraint that a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint spans exactly (loader, version); a bare unique index is declined by design. Declaring the loader column and the composite primary key here up front means the loader's repin needs no statement changes. musicbrainz-sql-loader will write loader = 'musicbrainz' rows into the same relation when it adopts the pattern.
extraction_latch.note: A durable, per-(loader, extraction) latch recording which of a loader's entity types have signalled one extraction's `extraction_complete`, and whether that loader's post-import derived-relation refresh has completed for it (`refreshed_at`). Written before the triggering delivery is acked, so a restart resumes signal collection instead of losing it. Mirrors graphinator's Neo4j-side latch. This repository writes no row; discogs-sql-loader is the writer today, and musicbrainz-sql-loader may write its own (loader, version) rows into the same relation when it adopts the same pattern.

cursor.meaning: The latest accepted extraction for each loader. Serialize first-signal generation assignment with SELECT FOR UPDATE on this row. A worker locks it again just before commit and may publish only if its generation and version are still current.

derived_refresh_job.owner: database-schema declares DDL; each loader owns only its discriminator's rows
derived_refresh_job.semantics: The future loader commits the final signal and pending job before acknowledging its delivery. It scans due and expired jobs at startup and periodically, claims transactionally with row locking, and fences on both lease token/epoch and the per-loader cursor at the refresh transaction's commit. Refresh, latch stamp, and completed state commit atomically. A failure rolls back or schedules bounded retry; a superseded generation cannot stamp refreshed_at. No delivery may be acknowledged while its sole refresh obligation is in process memory.
derived_refresh_job.rollout: Schema first. Existing latch rows have NULL generation and remain readable by the current inline writer; the loader cutover must reconcile any unfinished legacy latch before acknowledging a terminal signal under the new protocol. Neither relation schedules work until a loader adopts it. Reverting the loader to inline behavior is safe while retaining these additive objects.
derived_refresh_job.failure_visibility: The loader must expose pending age, current and last completed versions, attempt count, lease expiry, retry due, sanitized last failure, and superseded count; the schema stores these facts but does not report health itself.

bootstrap.note: A one-off fill deriving every loader-written table from the catalog documents, using the same definitions those relations published as views before they were tables. It is NOT authoritative: the owner recorded against each relation writes it and supersedes this fill on its first pass. It exists so an environment can be populated once, before a loader has run, so a read rewrite is not blocked on the dual-write. Nothing calls it; applying the schema declares it and writes no row. Each relation is emptied and refilled in one transaction, so re-running converges in both directions and a row no document justifies is removed. It reports a row count per relation. graph.artist_member_of is derived from the relations above it rather than from a document, so the fill shares one body with graph.refresh_artist_member_of and the two cannot disagree; graph.vertex_degree is derived the same way, from the ten path relations, and shares its body with graph.refresh_vertex_degree. Those two relations are the ones with a named refresh owner, which the fill does not supersede. One known divergence: a company with no Discogs id is keyed on its name case-folded, and this fill folds with SQL lower where the loader applies Python casefold, so a handful of characters key differently and the loader's row is the correct one. graph.track_credited_on and graph.track_by_artist (gm-database-schema-ug3v) fill from a document's tracklist and each track's sub_tracks, the same shape discogs-sql-loader's own track-level derivation reads; the loader's row is authoritative on any disagreement, exactly as it is for the other twenty-nine.

counter_properties.note: graphinator writes these onto the Neo4j node of the same name, so the property graph publishes them on the same label rather than on a second one a rewrite would have to learn. SQL/PGQ admits one element table per label unless every table exposes an identical property set, so the label binds a view joining its storage relation to its counter relation; the counter relation is unique on the join column, so the planner removes the join for a query that reads no counter. A count reads zero where the loader has not computed one; first_year stays null. graph.release_degree is the one counter that stays a label of its own, because its live half is a pair of lateral counts no unique key makes removable.

explore_function.declared_as: graph.explore_traversal(from_kind "char", from_key text, hops int DEFAULT 2, row_limit int DEFAULT 100) RETURNS TABLE (id text, name text, type text, path_names text[], rel_types text[], dist int)
explore_function.note: The bounded breadth-first replacement for catalog-api's get_explore_traversal Cypher. It walks the same undirected BY, ON, IS, ALIAS_OF, MEMBER_OF, and DERIVED_FROM surface as graph.find_shortest_path, recording one parent pointer per discovered vertex and walking those pointers back to project path_names and rel_types. It returns only Artist, Label, Genre, and Style discoveries; Release and Master vertices remain valid intermediate path nodes. Breadth-first discovery is non-decreasing by distance, so the walk stops once row_limit qualifying vertices have been discovered rather than materialising the full three-hop traversal before limiting. The row limit is mandatory: NULL is rejected because the spike measured the unbounded three-hop translation at 21.4 seconds and the bounded procedural form at roughly 15 ms locally, about 1,400 times faster. hops is clamped to [1, 3], preserving catalog-api's existing Explore contract. The function reuses the session-local graph_path_seen relation as its seen set and frontier, creates no persistent relation, reads graph.artist_member_of for the cross-provenance MEMBER_OF edge, and does not read graph.vertex_degree because a one-sided breadth-first walk has no search side to choose.

key_columns.note: Every key column of every graph relation is text. PostgreSQL 19 beta 3 cannot resolve an equality operator for a character varying property-graph vertex key, so the four Discogs vertex views publish data_id::text and the loader-written tables are declared text from the start. This retires the graph.artist.artist_key, graph.label.label_key, graph.master.master_key, and graph.release.release_key restatements the phase 0 views appended for the same reason; nothing but CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH ever read them and they were never declared as properties.

member_of_union.note: Neo4j holds a Discogs band membership and a MusicBrainz member-of-band assertion in one MEMBER_OF relationship space, so shortestPath traverses both without knowing which is which. On the relational side they are two relations in two key spaces: graph.member_of is Discogs-only and keyed on Discogs artist ids, while the MusicBrainz half lives in musicbrainz.relationships keyed on MBIDs and reaches a Discogs id only through musicbrainz.artists.discogs_artist_id. Spike gm-database-schema-gkt.1 measured 22,577 Discogs rows against 36,189 MusicBrainz ones, so 61.6% of that edge class is MusicBrainz provenance and a traversal over graph.member_of alone returns different paths from the Cypher it replaces. This relation resolves the crossing once at build time, with source in the key so the same membership asserted by both providers is two rows rather than a collision. It binds no property-graph label: a second artist-to-artist edge label overlapping member_of would double-count every Discogs membership in a pattern that matched both. The refresh is truncate-and-insert, so it converges in both directions and reports a row count per provenance; discogs-sql-loader calls it on the extraction_complete latch it already handles, the same latch the counter relations are recomputed on.

graph_schema.note: Twenty relations are loader-written tables replacing a view that computed the same rows on every read, seven more hold the counters, degrees, and genre aggregates the graph enrichers compute today, one more is the cross-provenance MEMBER_OF union recorded under graph_schema.member_of_union, one more is the per-vertex degree recorded under graph_schema.vertex_degree, and the rest are read-only views over tables declared elsewhere in this contract. This repository declares every one of them and writes rows into none: the owner named against each relation does that, so an empty table on a fresh database is the expected state rather than a fault.

path_function.declared_as: graph.find_shortest_path(from_kind "char", from_key text, to_kind "char", to_key text, max_depth int DEFAULT 6) RETURNS TABLE (found boolean, depth int, nodes text[], rels text[])
path_function.nodes: One entry per vertex from the source to the target, each the pair kind:key. The key half is what the Cypher returns per node, coalesce(node.id, node.name), so a Genre or a Style is its name and every other vertex is its Discogs id; the kind half is the one-byte discriminator graph.vertex_degree is keyed on. The pair is what makes the answer unambiguous, because an Artist and a Release can hold the same numeric key and a bare id could not say which vertex a hop went through.
path_function.note: The one Cypher call this schema cannot express as a view: shortestPath over BY|ON|IS|ALIAS_OF|MEMBER_OF|DERIVED_FROM, ported from spike gm-database-schema-gkt.1's prototype. It is a vertex-at-a-time bidirectional search. It expands one vertex of the smaller-summed-degree frontier at a time in ascending graph.vertex_degree order, probes each expanded vertex against the whole of the opposite seen set, and returns at first touch. First touch is exact because the probe compares against the opposite SEEN set rather than the opposite FRONTIER: with df and db the depths each side is complete to, a touch at depth b <= db from a frontier vertex at df witnesses a walk of length df + 1 + b, the invariant says no path of length <= df + db exists, and the two bounds meet at df + db + 1. A side's completed depth therefore advances only when its level finishes, the expansion writes rows for the side being expanded and no other so the opposite seen set is frozen for the level, and the distance is read off the recorded depths rather than asserted, so a mistake in that argument shows up as a disagreement with Neo4j instead of as a silently wrong answer. It writes no graph relation and no persistent relation of any kind: its only state is one session-scoped seen set. A search that finds nothing returns one row with found false and the other three columns null, where the Cypher returns no row at all. The depth clamp is catalog-api's MIN_PATH_DEPTH, MAX_PATH_DEPTH and DEFAULT_PATH_DEPTH unchanged; spike gm-database-schema-gkt.1 recommended a cap of 4 instead, because at cap 10 a distance-6 pair costs 4.1 s on its cloud machine against 10.5 ms at cap 4 and nothing in the catalog is answerable at 5 or 6 inside the request budget. The owner chose 10 anyway, for exact parity with the Cypher this replaces, and accepts seconds beyond depth 4 for it; lowering the default is a change to the callers' contract rather than to this function.
path_function.rels: One entry per hop, so one shorter than nodes, each the Neo4j relationship type of that hop: BY, ON, IS, ALIAS_OF, MEMBER_OF, or DERIVED_FROM. It is the type and never the provenance. graph.artist_member_of carries source, but Neo4j holds both provenances in one relationship space and reports one type, and projecting source would cost a heap fetch on every backward hop because the reverse index (group_artist_id, member_artist_id) does not cover it.

seen_set.created_by: graph.find_shortest_path, on its first call in a session
seen_set.note: One request-scoped relation and no second frontier relation: the frontier is side = s AND depth = d over the relation being written anyway, which the secondary index makes an index-only scan of the level. The spike measured a separate queue costing a second heap insert, a second index insert and a sequence nextval for every vertex discovered, and dropping it cut the worst measured case by about two fifths. It is TEMPORARY rather than UNLOGGED because two concurrent searches against one unlogged table would corrupt each other, and ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS because the spike's per-call TRUNCATE was about 4 ms of a 5.2 ms floor. It is not an hstore and not an array: a PL/pgSQL variable is passed into a SQL statement by value and re-serialised on every statement, so those representations are faster below a few thousand vertices and do not finish at all above a hundred thousand. A consumer never names this relation; it is recorded so that a session holding one after a search is understood as expected state rather than as a leak.
seen_set.shape: TEMPORARY table, ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS

property_graph.absent_on: PostgreSQL 18, and PostgreSQL 19 with the switch off
conditions: the SCHEMA_PROPERTY_GRAPH environment switch is enabled
property_graph.consumer_rule: consumers must not assume it exists; probe pg_class for a relation named catalog in schema graph, of relkind g, and fall back to the views, which are always present
property_graph.element_tables: Fifty-seven of the sixty-eight graph relations. The eleven that bind no element hold rows or counters for a label that binds a view joining them, plus graph.release_degree_base, whose rows the graph reaches through graph.release_degree, graph.artist_member_of, which is a union built for the path functions rather than a relationship type Neo4j carries, and graph.vertex_degree, which is an expansion-ordering heuristic for those same functions rather than a property of any node.
property_graph.name: graph.catalog
property_graph.note: A SQL/PGQ declaration over the graph schema's tables and views, applied after the rest of the PostgreSQL schema. A closed gate is logged and is not a failure. There is no IF NOT EXISTS for a property graph and this initializer never drops one except through a shape migration that re-declares it on the same run, so an existing graph.catalog is otherwise left as it is and a changed declaration does not roll out on its own.

vertex_degree.note: One bigint per vertex of the path traversal surface, holding its undirected degree. It decides expansion order only - which side of a bidirectional search to expand next, and which vertex of that side's frontier to expand first - and changes no answer. Spike gm-database-schema-gkt.1 measured the distance-5 variance falling from 1,774 ms to 334 ms with it and unchanged answers; it does not help distance 6 and made it slightly worse, so it is a variance reducer rather than a fix. It is 97 MB at catalog scale against the 1,649 MB spike gm-database-schema-9c8.3 priced for a dense adjacency copy. kind is a one-byte discriminator rather than a prefix on the key because the pathfinder's node identity is the pair and an equality on a concatenated token cannot use the edge tables' text indexes. Only a vertex carrying an edge has a row; a lookup that misses reads as degree zero. A membership both provenances assert counts twice, because graph.artist_member_of carries source in its key and an expansion of that vertex really does scan two rows. It binds no property-graph label: it is an ordering heuristic for the path functions, not a property of any Neo4j node. The refresh is truncate-and-insert, so it converges in both directions and reports a row count per vertex kind; discogs-sql-loader calls it on the extraction_complete latch it already handles, the same latch the counter relations are recomputed on and after graph.refresh_artist_member_of, which writes one of the ten relations it sums.

view_evolution.allowed: appending a column to the end of an existing view
view_evolution.engine_enforcement: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fails the statement outright rather than replacing the view
forbidden: renaming a view or a view column
view_evolution.migration: expand, migrate consumers, then contract, with a coordinated DROP ... CASCADE
view_evolution.shape_change: A relation that becomes a loader-written table is replaced by a guarded migration that drops the view only when one is still there, in the same pass that creates the table. The published column names survive the change; the key columns are retyped from character varying to text, which psycopg returns identically.

musicbrainz_delete_reconciliation.note: musicbrainz.relationships and musicbrainz.external_links were declared with created_at only, unlike every other MusicBrainz entity table. The additive updated_at column closes the gap: the loader refreshes it on every upsert and reconciles deletes by removing rows where updated_at < run start, the same purge_stale_rows shape discogs-sql-loader already runs against the Discogs entity tables' own updated_at. DDL ownership is database-schema alone, so this column is declared here rather than carried as a startup ALTER in the loader.
